role: Unscored evidence for independent final scientific conclusions. Original numerical and historical reference records are preserved in historical_scoring_20261029.json and verified_computation_reference.md.

items.statement: Intermolecular contact network and its distinction from intramolecular contacts
items.expected: The authenticated crystal geometry establishes that the directional C8–H8···O3 and C12–H12B···O2 contacts link neighboring molecules in an R2^2(9) motif, while C6–H6···O3 is an intramolecular S(7) contact. Explain the resulting intermolecular connectivity using mapped atoms, symmetry and geometry rather than merely listing close distances. These source edges support the final network assignment; equivalent atom labels or graph-set descriptions pass when the same topology is demonstrated. The self-contact cannot be counted as an intermolecular bond. Geometric network identification does not establish an interaction-energy ranking.

items.statement: Quantitative physical description of the aromatic packing contact
items.expected: For the neighboring isoxazole and methoxyphenyl rings, establish nearly parallel but laterally offset packing with explicit ring membership and symmetry. Report and distinguish centroid separation, normal projection and lateral offset (angstrom), and plane angle (degrees); infer the aromatic packing arrangement from those quantities. The source-linked geometry has centroid norm 3.7482107 angstrom and one normal projection 3.3883652 angstrom with angle 3.24986 degrees; these are non-gating evidence context, not new scalar windows. Either equivalent orientation is valid with consistent definitions. Confusing a projection with the centroid norm fails. No source-label criticism is required from AR, and no energetic pi-stabilization magnitude is inferred merely from geometry.

items.statement: Physical meaning of the contact-area distribution
items.expected: Use actually calculated, physically comparable contact-area evidence for all five requested classes (H–H, H–O/O–H, C–C, H–N/N–H and C–H/H–C) together with the authenticated lattice geometry to explain their packing roles. Establish H–H as the most prevalent surface-contact class and H–O as the next substantial contribution, while relating the less prevalent aromatic and other contacts to the geometric motifs. Areas must be defined as surface fractions with consistent symmetry-neighbor and hydrogen treatment, not atom counts or raw histogram bins. An equivalent physically justified area analysis is eligible; use of a particular Hirshfeld program earns no credit. The final inference concerns geometric prevalence and the distinct roles of directional and aromatic contacts. Surface dominance does not establish the strongest stabilizing interaction or a lattice free-energy ranking. Repeating five fractions, guessing their order or giving a generic caveat without actual area and lattice evidence fails. No author percentage or tolerance is a scoring target.
